# 1. Defining objects in R

We consider two vectors, $x$ and $y$:

$x=(1.9,1.2,0.7,2.7,1.2,3.1,2.3,2.1,2.1,1.4)$ and $y=(1.8,1.1,0.6,2.7,1.4,3.0,2.5,1.9,1.8,1.4)$.

We define the two vectors in R in the following way. For $x$:

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
x<-c(1.9,1.2,0.7,2.7,1.2,3.1,2.3,2.1,2.1,1.4)
x
```

and for $y$:

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
y<-c(1.8,1.1,0.6,2.7,1.4,3.0,2.5,1.9,1.8,1.4)
y
```



# 2. Calculate the mean of $x$ and $y$ in R

Our first data analysis task is to calculate the mean of $x$ and $y$. In R, the function <tt>mean()</tt> can be used to calculate the sample mean. In our example we use <tt>mean(x)</tt> and <tt>mean(y)</tt>:

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
mean(x)
mean(y)
```

# 3. Correlation between $x$ and $y$

Our second data analysis task is to calculate and visualize the correlation between $x$ and $y$. To calculate the correlation we use the function <tt>cor()</tt>.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
cor(x,y)
```

We use the function <tt>plot</tt> to produce the scatterplot.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
plot(x,y)
```

# 4. User functions

A function is R. is a code that can be used to produce output. For example, suppose that we want to calculate (1) the mean of two vectors, (2) the correlation between two vectors and (3) to plot a scatterplot. We can write a R function, <tt>discript</tt> that can be used to produce the output.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
discript<-function(x,y)
{
print(mean(x))
print(mean(y))
print(cor(x,y))
plot(x,y)
}
```

To apply the function to the the vectors $x$ and $y$ we use <tt>discript(x,y)</tt>.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
discript(x,y)
```

# 5. The cars dataset

The <tt>cars</tt> dataset contains information about cars' speed and cars' stoping distance. 

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
head(cars)
```

The first column is the cars' speed and the second column is the cars' stoping distance. Our data analysis task is

  * Calculate the mean of the cars' speed.
  * Calculate the mean of the cars' stopping distance.
  * Calculate the corelation between cars' speed and stopping distance and produce    a scaterplot.
  

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
discript(cars[,1],cars[,2])
```
